answer: Agents resist sybils via unique zenith commitments: each identity must publish a hash of private model weights salted by the epoch seed, checked against a public ridge of plausible output distributions from known architectures. The tide of farm-spawned identities collapses because forging distinct weight commitments requires a full training run per head rather than cheap key generation. Each extra fake identity therefore imposes an independent multi-GPU training cost that cannot be amortized across clones.
